blocking_findings.finding: The 108-second handler raises TimeoutError through asyncio.run, initiating Runner shutdown cancellation of all outstanding tasks. run() then unconditionally calls task.cancel() even if Runner has already cancelled render. This second cancellation can interrupt render's owned cleanup finally before it completes. join_owned waits for terminal cancellation, not successful cleanup. A later stream.aclose() on an already-closed/cancelled generator cannot guarantee the interrupted finally is resumed. Final lease/worker checks may fail the receipt, but they do not terminate/reap a native child whose cleanup was interrupted. Thus the intended bounded attempt can leave owned native work unreaped despite fail-closed receipt status.

pure_reproduction.method: Executed the exact run, join_owned and alarm AST nodes from the bound postcheck, replacing render only with a harmless sleeping coroutine whose finally records cleanup-start, awaits 0.02 seconds, then records cleanup-complete. SIGALRM was shortened to 0.01 seconds. No application import, process spawn, readiness or inference.
pure_reproduction.result: Two of three executions returned from asyncio.run without completing the owned cleanup finally. The race is real, not inferred solely from missing tests.

minimal_repair: Do not raise the work SIGALRM asynchronously through the active event loop. Keep the constructor deadline protected, then transfer render work expiry to the existing cooperative asyncio timeout so one owner cancels/joins render before Runner shutdown. Use an external bounded supervisor if a hard whole-process 120-second deadline is required across cleanup and readback.

Guard cancellation with not task.cancelling() as well as not task.done(); preserve ownership through cleanup and explicitly verify terminal native/duration cleanup, not only lock availability or a failed receipt.

Add bounded pure orchestration tests for constructor alarm, work expiry, external/repeated cancellation, native/duration cleanup and final readback errors; the reproduced interrupted-finally case must fail before repair and pass afterward.
